title: Revealing Deformation Mechanism in Disordered Materials using 4D STEM
content: Metallic glasses (MGs) are an exciting class of materials due to their unique mechanical and functional properties. Still, potential applications are hindered by their limited ductility caused by the formation of shear bands leading to catastrophic failure. A fundamental understanding of the shear banding process is key for improving the mechanical properties of MGs. While progress on the understanding of deformation localization was made using atomistic simulations, highlighting the importance of nanoscale structural variations and local elastic strains for the initiation and propagation of shear bands, direct experimental studies are scarce. In crystalline metals and alloys dislocations can be imaged using transmission electron microscopy (TEM). In contrast to that, the disordered nature of MGs hinders direct imaging of the atomic structure in the TEM inhibiting uncovering the fundamental deformation mechanisms at the nanoscale.
